product_target.statement: Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate delivered in this repository through public crate interfaces and a minimal non-game validation executable; this repository does not deliver a particular game.

documents.rationale: Repository overview that points to the mixed program brief as the product definition and labels the interface reference as supporting technical context; it does not independently set product scope.
States the current Moria substrate product boundary, public API, correctness and validation commitments, non-goals, and explicitly marks Product One content as later-consumer vision.
Describes the reusable public surface downstream consumers need and states that it does not add deliverables.

claims.statement: Moria is the reusable voxel-world substrate defined by docs/seeds/mixed-project-brief.md; the brief includes a later-product vision inside an otherwise binding current-product document, and only the current substrate commitments are deliverables in this repository.
docs/seeds/substrate-interface-reference.md supplies supporting technical context without expanding product scope.

Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate consumed through public crate interfaces by games and by a minimal validation executable; this repository delivers the substrate, not any particular game.

The current product owns deterministic seed-based generation, sparse voxel storage, bounded streaming, mutation, surface extraction, persistence, and read-only diagnostics; these capabilities must remain useful to multiple downstream consumers.
Generation is deterministic for the same versioned parameters and seed.

External consumers can create and identify a world, request bounded regions, observe readiness, query material truth, submit bounded edits, and persist deltas, and must not reach into storage, meshing, or scheduler internals.

The validation executable uses exactly the public interfaces, may provide a free-fly camera and diagnostics sufficient to exercise the crate, is not a game prototype, and owns no privileged world path.

Mutation is admitted through a bounded command API and committed atomically; persistence restores the same authoritative material state; derived meshes and diagnostics never become authoritative world state; streaming bounds resident work and exposes observable lifecycle states; failures remain typed and observable.

Headless fixtures cover generation, query, mutation, persistence, and lifecycle behavior; a small visual fixture demonstrates that a relocated external consumer can render and edit through the public API; performance is reported with machine identity without a machine-specific correctness threshold.

Moria does not implement game rules, combat, inventory, AI, narrative systems, characters, animation, authored levels, or production content; references to possible consumers explain interface pressure only.

After the reusable substrate ships, a separate Product One repository may place a third-person explorer in a generated region; those later paragraphs are future-consumer context and do not authorize a player controller, character mesh, animation clips, curated route, or game asset in Moria.

A later Product One consumer vision may include a dense mixed forest (with hills, a river, and a cave) in a generated region; that forest population workload is future-consumer context and is not authorized as a Moria deliverable.

The later consumer vision paragraphs are future-consumer context embedded in this binding program brief and do not authorize a player controller, character mesh, animation clips, forest population workload, curated route, or game asset in Moria.
This reference supports the Moria program brief, describes the reusable surface that downstream consumers need, and does not add deliverables.

The reusable surface covers world identity, readiness and material queries, bounded mutations with admission failures and commit revisions, streaming lifecycle states, authoritative persistence deltas, registered objects that are not game entities, and diagnostics without mutable internal handles.
